newsitem.title: LEBANON: Ceasefire monitors deplore Lebanon casualty.
newsitem.headline: Ceasefire monitors deplore Lebanon casualty.

text.p: A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire in Lebanon deplored the wounding of a Lebanese civilian in a guerrilla car bomb explosion in south Lebanon last Monday.
The group comprising the United States, France, Israel, Syria and Lebanon urged in a statement issued late on Thursday that south Lebanon combatants avoid civilian targets.

"The Monitoring Group acknowledged as factual that a car bomb was detonated by a Lebanese armed group on March 10, 1997, in proximity to an inhabited house on the road between Marqaba and Houla resulting in at least one civilian being treated for shock and causing damage to the house and a civilian vehicle, and deplored these consequences," the group said in a statement.

The group had ended been discussing an Israeli complaint over the attack, in which a guerrilla detonated a car bomb as an Israeli patrol drove past on the road in the central sector of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
Two Lebanese children were lightlty wounded and a woman was treated for shock according to pro-Israeli militia sources.
No group claimed responsiblity for the attack.
"The Monitoring Group once again strongly urged responsible authorities to ensure strict observance of the provisions of the April 26, 1996 understanding," the group said.
Under a U.S.-brokered understanding that ended 17 days of an Israeli onslaught on Lebanon, Israel and Hizbollah are banned from firing from or at civilian targets on both sides of the border.
